title: Energy resources
examples: What is the difference between renewable and non-renewable energy sources?
Can you give me an example of a clean energy source?
What are the main disadvantages of using oil for power?

explain.say: Today we will explore different energy sources around us. We will learn what makes them renewable or non-renewable.
Renewable energy comes from sources that will naturally keep coming back. These sources will not run out over a short time.
Non-renewable energy comes from sources that exist in limited amounts. Once we use them up, they take millions of years to form again.

items: Millions of years ago: Fossil fuels formed
Today: We are using them up

explain.say: A pro of solar power is that it produces zero pollution when it runs. This is good for the air we breathe.
A con of burning coal is that it releases harmful gases into the atmosphere. This contributes to climate change.
In everyday life, many cities are switching to electric buses powered by renewable sources. This helps clean the air for everyone.

faq.a: Yes, coal, oil, and natural gas are all considered non-renewable resources. They formed over vast amounts of time from ancient organic matter.
asks: Are coal and gas the same type of energy?

faq.q: Can wind power be completely clean?
faq.a: While running wind turbines produce no emissions, the manufacturing and placement of the turbines do have an environmental impact.
asks: What are the downsides of using wind energy?

faq.q: Does the sun run out of energy?
faq.a: The sun is a star, and it is not expected to run out of energy for billions of years. For our purposes, we consider it a vast, sustainable source.
asks: How long will the sun shine?

faq.q: What is the biggest advantage of using renewable energy?
faq.a: The biggest advantage is that using these sources helps to reduce greenhouse gases, which helps to keep the planet stable for future generations.
asks: Why is renewable energy better for the planet?
What is the main benefit of solar power?

faq.q: Are there any non-renewable sources that are also clean?
faq.a: Generally, no. Burning any fossil fuel releases carbon dioxide, which is a greenhouse gas. Nuclear power is different but has its own waste concerns.
asks: Is natural gas cleaner than coal?
Can we burn something that is not fossil fuel?

facts: Solar energy captures light and heat from the sun.
Wind energy converts the kinetic energy of moving air into electricity.
Fossil fuels, like oil and coal, are formed from ancient plants and animals.
A key benefit of renewables is their low impact on air quality.

quiz.say: Which pair represents one renewable and one non-renewable resource?
quiz.why: Wind is constantly replenished by the atmosphere, making it renewable. Oil is a finite fossil fuel, making it non-renewable.

wrong.0: Uranium is used in nuclear power, which is not classified as a simple fossil fuel, but the pair is not the best fit.
wrong.2: Both options are incorrect because coal is a non-renewable fossil fuel.
wrong.3: Gas is a non-renewable fossil fuel, even though water can be a source of energy.

quiz.say: If a country relies heavily on burning coal for electricity, what is the main environmental consequence?
quiz.why: Burning coal releases large amounts of carbon dioxide and other pollutants, which traps heat in the atmosphere.

wrong.0: Although pollution can cause smells, the primary scientific concern is the gas emissions affecting the climate.
wrong.1: Cost is an economic factor, but the direct physical impact of burning coal is atmospheric pollution.
wrong.3: While it is finite, the immediate consequence of burning it is pollution, not just running out.

quiz.say: Which energy source has the best balance of low emissions and continuous availability?
quiz.why: Solar power is renewable and, when installed correctly, produces very little pollution during operation.

wrong.0: Natural gas is still a fossil fuel and releases greenhouse gases when burned.
wrong.1: Coal releases significantly more pollutants than solar power during combustion.
wrong.2: Oil is a fossil fuel and its combustion releases harmful gases into the atmosphere.
